units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus according to the commandment of God our Saviour, and Christ Jesus our hope;

units.leftText: To Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. Correcting False Teachers (Titus 1:10–16|TIT 1:10-16*)
units.rightText: unto Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: As I urged you on my departure to Macedonia, you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines
units.rightText: As I exhorted thee to tarry at Ephesus, when I was going into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge certain men not to teach a different doctrine,

units.leftText: or devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation rather than the stewardship of God’s work, which is by faith.
units.rightText: neither to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questionings, rather than a dispensation of God which is in faith; so do I now.
leftNotes: 1:4 Literally rather than the stewardship of God in faith

units.leftText: The goal of our instruction is the love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.
units.rightText: But the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned:

units.leftText: Some have strayed from these ways and turned aside to empty talk.
units.rightText: from which things some having swerved have turned aside unto vain talking;

units.leftText: They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert.
units.rightText: desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say, nor whereof they confidently affirm.

units.leftText: Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it legitimately.
units.rightText: But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully,

units.leftText: We realize that law is not enacted for the righteous, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinful, for the unholy and profane, for killers of father or mother, for murderers,
units.rightText: as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and unruly, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,

units.leftText: for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave traders and liars and perjurers, and for anyone else who is averse to sound teaching
units.rightText: for fornicators, for abusers of themselves with men, for menstealers, for liars, for false swearers, and if there be any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine;

units.leftText: that agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted. God’s Grace to Paul
units.rightText: according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.

units.leftText: I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service.
units.rightText: I thank him that enabled me, even Christ Jesus our Lord, for that he counted me faithful, appointing me to his service;

units.leftText: I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man; yet because I had acted in ignorance and unbelief, I was shown mercy.
units.rightText: though I was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: howbeit I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief;

units.leftText: And the grace of our Lord overflowed to me, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: and the grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief:

units.leftText: But for this very reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, the worst of sinners, Christ Jesus might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
units.rightText: howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me as chief might Jesus Christ show forth all his longsuffering, for an ensample of them that should thereafter believe on him unto eternal life.

units.leftText: Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
units.rightText: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: Timothy, my child, I entrust you with this command in keeping with the previous prophecies about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,
units.rightText: This charge I commit unto thee, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which led the way to thee, that by them thou mayest war the good warfare;

units.leftText: holding on to faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and thereby shipwrecked their faith.
units.rightText: holding faith and a good conscience; which some having thrust from them made shipwreck concerning the faith:

units.leftText: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan to be taught not to blaspheme.
units.rightText: of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I delivered unto Satan, that they might be taught not to blaspheme.

units.leftText: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone—
units.rightText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, be made for all men;

units.leftText: for kings and all those in authority— so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.
units.rightText: for kings and all that are in high place; that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and gravity.

units.leftText: This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior,
units.rightText: This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;

units.leftText: who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
units.rightText: who would have all men to be saved, and come to the knowledge of the truth.

units.leftText: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: For there is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: who gave Himself as a ransom for all — the testimony that was given at just the right time.
units.rightText: who gave himself a ransom for all; the testimony to be borne in its own times;

units.leftText: For this reason I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a faithful and true teacher of the Gentiles. I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything.
units.rightText: whereunto I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I speak the truth, I lie not), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

units.leftText: Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension. Instructions to Women
units.rightText: I desire therefore that the men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and disputing.

units.leftText: Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with respectable apparel, with modesty, and with self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes,
units.rightText: In like manner, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefastness and sobriety; not with braided hair, and gold or pearls or costly raiment;

units.leftText: but with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God.
units.rightText: but (which becometh women professing godliness) through good works.

units.leftText: A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.
units.rightText: Let a woman learn in quietness with all subjection.

units.leftText: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.
units.rightText: But I permit not a woman to teach, nor to have dominion over a man, but to be in quietness.

units.leftText: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.
units.rightText: For Adam was first formed, then Eve;

units.leftText: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.
units.rightText: and Adam was not beguiled, but the woman being beguiled hath fallen into transgression:

units.leftText: Women, however, will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.
units.rightText: but she shall be saved through her child-bearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with sobriety.
leftNotes: 2:15 Literally She, however, will be saved

units.leftText: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, If a man seeketh the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

units.leftText: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
units.rightText: The bishop therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, orderly, given to hospitality, apt to teach;
leftNotes: 3:2 Or faithful to his wife; also in verse 12

units.leftText: not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.
units.rightText: no brawler, no striker; but gentle, not contentious, no lover of money;

units.leftText: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.
units.rightText: one that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;

units.leftText: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?
units.rightText: (but if a man knoweth not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)

units.leftText: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.
units.rightText: not a novice, lest being puffed up he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

units.leftText: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil. Qualifications for Deacons (Acts 6:1–7|ACT 6:1-7*)
units.rightText: Moreover he must have good testimony from them that are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

units.leftText: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.
units.rightText: Deacons in like manner must be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;

units.leftText: They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
units.rightText: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.

units.leftText: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.
units.rightText: And let these also first be proved; then let them serve as deacons, if they be blameless.

units.leftText: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.
units.rightText: Women in like manner must be grave, not slanderers, temperate, faithful in all things.

units.leftText: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.
units.rightText: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.

units.leftText: For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus. The Mystery of Godliness
units.rightText: For they that have served well as deacons gain to themselves a good standing, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things
units.rightText: These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly;

units.leftText: in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
units.rightText: but if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how men ought to behave themselves in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

units.leftText: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
units.rightText: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness; He who was manifested in the flesh, Justified in the spirit, Seen of angels, Preached among the nations, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.
leftNotes: 3:16 Literally He who appeared; BYZ and TR God appeared

units.leftText: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons,
units.rightText: But the Spirit saith expressly, that in later times some shall fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,

units.leftText: influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
units.rightText: through the hypocrisy of men that speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron;

units.leftText: They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
units.rightText: forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by them that believe and know the truth.

units.leftText: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,
units.rightText: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it be received with thanksgiving:

units.leftText: because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer. A Good Servant of Jesus Christ
units.rightText: for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.

units.leftText: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.
units.rightText: If thou put the brethren in mind of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith, and of the good doctrine which thou hast followed until now:

units.leftText: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
units.rightText: but refuse profane and old wives’ fables. And exercise thyself unto godliness:

units.leftText: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
units.rightText: for bodily exercise is profitable for a little; but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life which now is, and of that which is to come.

units.leftText: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation.

units.leftText: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
units.rightText: For to this end we labor and strive, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of them that believe.
leftNotes: 4:10 SBL, BYZ, and TR and suffer reproach

units.leftText: Command and teach these things.
units.rightText: These things command and teach.

units.leftText: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
units.rightText: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an ensample to them that believe, in word, in manner of life, in love, in faith, in purity.

units.leftText: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
units.rightText: Till I come, give heed to reading, to exhortation, to teaching.

units.leftText: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
units.rightText: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

units.leftText: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
units.rightText: Be diligent in these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy progress may be manifest unto all.

units.leftText: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
units.rightText: Take heed to thyself, and to thy teaching. Continue in these things; for in doing this thou shalt save both thyself and them that hear thee.

units.leftText: Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father.
units.rightText: Rebuke not an elder, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brethren:

units.leftText: older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. Honoring True Widows (Ruth 1:1–5|RUT 1:1-5*)
units.rightText: the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.

units.leftText: Honor the widows who are truly widows.
units.rightText: Honor widows that are widows indeed.

units.leftText: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God.
units.rightText: But if any widow hath children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety towards their own family, and to requite their parents: for this is acceptable in the sight of God.

units.leftText: The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.
units.rightText: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, hath her hope set on God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.

units.leftText: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.
units.rightText: But she that giveth herself to pleasure is dead while she liveth.

units.leftText: Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.
units.rightText: These things also command, that they may be without reproach.

units.leftText: If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
units.rightText: But if any provideth not for his own, and specially his own household, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.

units.leftText: A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, faithful to her husband,
units.rightText: Let none be enrolled as a widow under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man,

units.leftText: and well known for good deeds such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.
units.rightText: well reported of for good works; if she hath brought up children, if she hath used hospitality to strangers, if she hath washed the saints’ feet, if she hath relieved the afflicted, if she hath diligently followed every good work.

units.leftText: But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry,
units.rightText: But younger widows refuse: for when they have waxed wanton against Christ, they desire to marry;

units.leftText: and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.
units.rightText: having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.

units.leftText: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.
units.rightText: And withal they learn also to be idle, going about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

units.leftText: So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.
units.rightText: I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, give no occasion to the adversary for reviling:

units.leftText: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
units.rightText: for already some are turned aside after Satan.

units.leftText: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need. Honoring Elders
units.rightText: If any woman that believeth hath widows, let her relieve them, and let not the church be burdened; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.

units.leftText: Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
units.rightText: Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.

units.leftText: For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
units.rightText: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn. And, The laborer is worthy of his hire.
leftNotes: 5:18 Luke 10:7|LUK 10:7*; see also Leviticus 19:13 and Deuteronomy 24:14–15.

units.leftText: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
units.rightText: Against an elder receive not an accusation, except at the mouth of two or three witnesses.

units.leftText: But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin. A Charge to Timothy
units.rightText: Them that sin reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.

units.leftText: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.
units.rightText: I charge thee in the sight of God, and Christ Jesus, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.

units.leftText: Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
units.rightText: Lay hands hastily on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.

units.leftText: Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
units.rightText: Be no longer a drinker of water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.

units.leftText: The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.
units.rightText: Some men’s sins are evident, going before unto judgment; and some men also they follow after.

units.leftText: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.
units.rightText: In like manner also there are good works that are evident; and such as are otherwise cannot be hid.

units.leftText: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.
units.rightText: Let as many as are servants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine be not blasphemed.

units.leftText: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved believers. Teach and encourage these principles. Reject False Doctrines
units.rightText: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but let them serve them the rather, because they that partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. These things teach and exhort.

units.leftText: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching,
units.rightText: If any man teacheth a different doctrine, and consenteth not to sound words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;

units.leftText: he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,
units.rightText: he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but doting about questionings and disputes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,

units.leftText: and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain. Godliness with Contentment
units.rightText: wranglings of men corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth, supposing that godliness is a way of gain.
leftNotes: 6:5 BYZ and TR include Withdraw yourself from such.

units.leftText: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.
units.rightText: But godliness with contentment is great gain:

units.leftText: For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.
units.rightText: for we brought nothing into the world, for neither can we carry anything out;

units.leftText: But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.
units.rightText: but having food and covering we shall be therewith content.

units.leftText: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.
units.rightText: But they that are minded to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and hurtful lusts, such as drown men in destruction and perdition.

units.leftText: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows. Fight the Good Fight
units.rightText: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil: which some reaching after have been led astray from the faith, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

units.leftText: But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
units.rightText: But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.

units.leftText: Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses.
units.rightText: Fight the good fight of the faith, lay hold on the life eternal, whereunto thou wast called, and didst confess the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.

units.leftText: I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate:
units.rightText: I charge thee in the sight of God, who giveth life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed the good confession;

units.leftText: Keep this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: that thou keep the commandment, without spot, without reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:

units.leftText: which the blessed and only Sovereign One— the King of kings and Lord of lords— will bring about in His own time.
units.rightText: which in its own times he shall show, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;

units.leftText: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen. A Charge to the Rich (Proverbs 23:1–5|PRO 23:1-5*; James 5:1–6|JAS 5:1-6*)
units.rightText: who only hath immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and power eternal. Amen.

units.leftText: Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
units.rightText: Charge them that are rich in this present world, that they be not highminded, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;

units.leftText: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share,
units.rightText: that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to communicate;

units.leftText: treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life. Guard the Faith
units.rightText: laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the life which is life indeed.

units.leftText: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid irreverent, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge,”
units.rightText: O Timothy, guard that which is committed unto thee, turning away from the profane babblings and oppositions of the knowledge which is falsely so called;

units.leftText: which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith. Grace be with you all.
units.rightText: which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you.
